commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Evict removed features on refresh; gate startup on first load (#27)

* Refresh README with current usage, container and docs overview

* Evict removed features on refresh; back cache with a ConcurrentMap

Replace the Spring CaffeineCache abstraction with a plain ConcurrentMap
(the live asMap() view of a Caffeine cache), keeping Caffeine confined to
infra and letting the application layer read/write the store directly.

CachingFeatureService becomes InMemoryFeatureService, now a Subscriber
fed by the load pipeline: per refresh tick it tracks the ids seen,
caches each parsed feature, and on tick completion evicts every cached
feature no longer present, so features deleted from the repository stop
being served on the next poll. A failed tick leaves the cache untouched;
the TTL remains as a backstop. Drop the now-unused spring-context-support
dependency.

FeatureLoader runs one tick immediately and then one per completed tick
plus a fixed delay (Mono.defer(tick).delayElement(refresh).repeat()), so
ticks never overlap even when a refresh is slow. Each read is wrapped in
Mono.defer(...).onErrorResume(...) so a single malformed file is skipped
without aborting the tick.

Tests: rename/extend InMemoryFeatureServiceTest with subscriber scenarios,
add FeatureLoaderTest for tickFlux, and add an integration scenario
deleting a feature from the origin repo and asserting a 404 after the
next refresh.

* Make integration tests order-independent without Thread.sleep

Remove @TestMethodOrder/@Order and replace polling sleep loops with
Awaitility, which spring-boot-starter-test already provides. The removal
test now creates and removes its own dedicated feature so no test mutates
state another test reads.

* Split refresh scheduling into infra; gate startup on first load

Move the fixed-delay refresh lifecycle out of the application layer:
FeatureLoader now exposes only Mono<Void> load(), while a new
FeatureRefreshScheduler (infra.scheduling) owns cadence and lifecycle.
The scheduler runs a first tick that blocks startup and retries with
exponential backoff (features.refresh.backoff.*, default PT1S/PT1M/5),
so the app is ready only once the cache is populated, then keeps a
fixed-delay loop whose ticks tolerate failures.

* Complete load Mono only after the cache is reconciled

The load pipeline emitted the done signal upstream of the cache sink, so
the returned Mono completed before InMemoryFeatureService.onComplete()
evicted removed features. Wrap the sink in a LoadRun subscriber that
forwards every signal first and only then completes the Mono, and cover
the ordering with a regression test.

* Refactor refresh scheduler as SmartLifecycle with configurable timeouts

* Document that load completes only after cache reconciliation

commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Shallow Git clones to improve startup time (#26)

* Refresh git clone via fetch + hard reset instead of pull

The local clone is a read-only mirror of the latest committed feature files,
so a merge-based pull is unnecessary and fails on shallow clones (no shared
history to compute a merge base). Fetch the tracked branch and hard-reset the
working tree to its remote tip, which works identically on full and shallow
clones.

* Clone the feature repo shallowly by default

Add a configurable clone depth (features.git.clone.depth, default 1) so the
startup clone transfers only the most recent commit instead of the full
history, reducing startup time. Set it to 0 for a full-history clone. The
depth is preserved across refresh fetches so the clone stays shallow.

JGit rejects setDepth(0), so depth is applied only when > 0.

* Document configurable shallow clone depth

* Document fetch+reset refresh and shallow clone in architecture docs

* Optimize clone and refresh in GitRepoManager

- Drop the lsRemote round-trip used to resolve the default branch before
  cloning; JGit's clone already checks out HEAD when no branch is set, so a
  branch override is only set when configured. Removes the HEAD-not-symbolic
  master fallback.
- Only reconcile the tracked branch when opening an existing clone; a fresh
  clone already checks out the tracked branch, so the call is a no-op there.
- Fetch only the tracked branch during update() via a branch-scoped refspec,
  reducing transfer on multi-branch repositories.

* Keep all fetches shallow and document the ls-remote clone narrowing

Apply the shallow clone depth to the branch-override reconciliation fetch so
restarting with a changed features.git.remote.branch does not transfer the new
branch's full history. Document that the ls-remote probe exists to name the
branch for branchesToClone, since JGit clones every remote branch otherwise.
Add tests asserting the clone is narrowed to the tracked branch only and stays
shallow across an override switch.

* Add debug logging for branch listing in GitRepoManager

commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Require git remote URL outside the dev profile (#24)

Remove the hardcoded development repository URI from application.yaml so
production never silently clones it. The URL is now mandatory in every
environment except local development: when missing, startup aborts with a
clear error naming features.git.remote.url. Local runs keep using the
development repository via the new dev profile (application-dev.yaml).

commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Reactive file repository: offload blocking I/O to boundedElastic (#22)

* Make local feature file scanning reactive

Offload the blocking filesystem enumeration (directory listing and file
attribute checks) to a bounded-elastic scheduler via Mono.fromCallable,
collecting listings with try-with-resources. Content reads stay on the
reactive DataBufferUtils.read path; file-name ordering is preserved with
flatMapSequential.

* Offload blocking git update to boundedElastic scheduler

* Document boundedElastic offloading in reactive data flow docs

* Manage DirectoryStream lifecycle with Flux.using

Replace Mono.fromCallable + try-with-resources with Flux.using (eager),
which closes each DirectoryStream on completion, downstream error, or
cancellation. The checked IOException from close() is unwrapped via a
small Consumer helper.

commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Add GitHub Actions release pipeline (#19) (#20)

* Add GitHub Actions release pipeline (#19)

- Add Release workflow (release.yml): workflow_dispatch + workflow_call,
  optional semver input (blank derives from gradle.properties), builds and
  publishes ghcr.io/ehpalumbo/feature-valves image (latest only from
  master), creates v<version> tag and GitHub Release, and opens a PR to
  bump the next snapshot version
- Move project version to gradle.properties; build.gradle reads it via
  Gradle convention and -Pversion overrides it for release builds
- Drop master-only image artifact save/upload from CI workflow; keep
  bootBuildImage as build validation
- Document the release process in docs/operations/release.md and update
  index and container-image docs

* Address release pipeline review comments (#20)

- Derive the image name from github.repository and keep it in a job-level
  IMAGE_NAME variable (registry in REGISTRY), instead of hardcoding
  ghcr.io/ehpalumbo/feature-valves
- Enable auto-generated release notes on the GitHub Release
- Replace the bump-PR with direct version commits pushed via a
  write-capable deploy key that bypasses the branch ruleset; commit the
  release version before tagging so v<version> points at a released
  version, then commit the next snapshot
- Drop pull-requests permission; gitignore the deploy key files

* Harden release workflow for idempotent reruns and pin version before build

commits.author: EH Palumbo
commits.message:
Add Docker image build via Spring Boot buildpacks with AOT processing (#6) (#18)

Build an OCI image with the bootBuildImage Gradle task (Paketo tiny/Ubuntu
Noble run image), applying the spring-boot-aot plugin so the JVM image runs
AOT-processed (spring.aot.enabled=true baked into JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS). Test AOT
is disabled as it is only needed for GraalVM native test runs.

CI builds the image in the existing build job on every run (reusing compiled
outputs) and docker-saves the image as an artifact on master only. JDK
distribution switched to Liberica to match the runtime JRE in the image.

Document the approach, base-image rationale, and run instructions in the README
and a new operations doc page.

Review comments (#13) noted the explicit no-arg constructors added for

Remove Guava: vanilla Java + Spring utils, records, Lombok, Caffeine cache (#10)

* Remove Guava in favor of vanilla Java, Spring utils, records, and Lombok

Replace the Guava dependency across main and tests: Guava's Cache is swapped
for Caffeine wrapped in Spring's CaffeineCache (same write-side TTL), pure
data carriers become Java records, behavior-bearing classes use Lombok, and
remaining API calls map to java.util and org.springframework.util equivalents.
Update embedded architecture docs to drop Guava references.

* Address review: inject cache via config class, Duration TTL, newlines, BOM cleanup

commits.message:
Upgrade to Spring Boot 4.1.0 / Spring Framework 7 / Gradle 9 / JDK 25 (#3)

* Add SIA for Spring Boot 4 upgrade with pre-upgrade test coverage gate

* Add implementation plan for Spring Boot 4 upgrade

* Add pre-upgrade test coverage gate for Spring Boot 4 upgrade

Author 44-test JUnit 4 suite on the current Boot 2.0.0.M4 / JDK 8 stack:
unit tests over the domain/engine, identifier and value objects, Jackson
POJOs, service/factory, and repository layers, plus a full-context
REST integration test (RANDOM_PORT + WebTestClient) driven by a real
local JGit repo. This suite is the no-regression proof for the Boot
4.1.0 jump.

Deviation from plan (approved): LocalFeatureFileRepository.filesOf
paired sorted ids with async flatMap reads via zipWith, which could
reorder buffers and made the pre-existing testLoadAll flaky. Rewritten
to a single-pass, order-preserving flatMapSequential.

Also corrects SIA finding #3: FeatureCheckRequest's single-arg
@JsonCreator(Map) is a delegate creator, so the request body is a flat
tag map, not {"tags":{...}}; tests and plan docs updated accordingly.

* Upgrade to Spring Boot 4.1.0 with JUnit Jupiter test migration

Phase 1 (Boot 4.1.0 / Gradle 9.7 / JDK 25):
- Rewrite build.gradle: plugins block, spring-boot-dependencies platform,
  implementation/testImplementation configurations, sourceCompatibility 25,
  useJUnitPlatform, remove io.spring.dependency-management and snapshot repos
- Regenerate Gradle wrapper to 9.7.0
- Replace removed DataBufferUtils.read(AsynchronousFileChannel, ...) overload
  with the Path-based read (LocalFeatureFileRepository)
- Refresh CI workflow to v4 actions on JDK 25 with gradle/actions/setup-gradle

Phase 2 (JUnit 4 -> Jupiter migration, zero assertion changes):
- Migrate all 12 test classes to JUnit Jupiter; TemporaryFolder -> @TempDir,
  syncBody -> bodyValue, drop SpringRunner
- Add spring-boot-webtestclient dependency; AutoConfigureWebTestClient moved to
  org.springframework.boot.webtestclient.autoconfigure in Boot 4
- Jackson 3: test mapper imports -> tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper
- Fix flat-map request contract on Jackson 3: explicit
  @JsonCreator(mode = DELEGATING) since single-arg @JsonCreator becomes
  property-based when compiled with -parameters
- Update plan README with Phase 2 corrections

Full ./gradlew build green on JDK 25 (44 tests, no assertion changes).

* Remove completed SIA and implementation plan docs

The Spring Boot 4.1.0 upgrade is delivered; drop the planning artifacts
and the stale index link.

* Modernize tests with text blocks, var, and final

* Update architecture docs for Spring Boot 4.1.0 and Java 25 upgrade

* Replace system properties with @DynamicPropertySource in integration test

* Bump version to 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT

* Publish test results to GitHub Actions
